machines.note: Independent Web-only reconstruction based on multiple public HTB Intense writeups. Real Flask + SQLite; reflected SQLite errors and a conditional error oracle extract the administrator secret; SHA-256 secret-prefix LWT signature length extension plus duplicate-key parsing for admin session; unchecked admin log path join reads the per-instance Web Flag. Original private source is not copied; observable route and exploit path are preserved. SNMP, SSH pivot and native pwn/root stages are intentionally excluded. Initial implementation only: no Docker build, manual acceptance, Worker verification or release yet.

challenge_model.principle: A Lab is a reusable runtime environment, not a one-to-one synonym for a Challenge. One Lab may host multiple Challenges; each Challenge may map to multiple Skills.

entities.lab: Deployable application/runtime, image, services, ports, resource/network constraints, lifecycle and reset boundary.
entities.challenge: Learner-facing objective, difficulty, prompt, hints, answer/Flag and completion state.
entities.lab_challenge: Many-to-many association between runtime Labs and Challenges, including entry point, shared-state and environment requirements.
entities.challenge_skill: Many-to-many association with one primary Skill and zero or more secondary Skills.
entities.challenge_dependency: Optional directed prerequisite relation between Challenges, justified by the real application flow.

rules: Do not create a new Docker image or runtime instance solely because a new Challenge is added to an existing Lab.
A Challenge can combine multiple Skills; one Skill can appear in multiple Challenges.
Split a composite application into multiple Challenges only when each has a distinct learner objective and defensible completion boundary.
Use prerequisite dependencies when the real application requires an earlier foothold; do not invent parallel entry points.
Each Challenge has its own answer/Flag and Web-backend grading record. Worker manages only Lab and sandbox lifecycle.
A shared Lab reset resets the shared environment and all Challenge progress tied to that instance unless independent snapshots are explicitly supported.
Web-only Challenges do not require SSH, Linux root or two Flags unless those are part of the actual stated objective.
Proposals do not imply existing Challenge files, separate Flag placement, independent exploitability or acceptance.
challenge_model.migration_policy: Keep existing machine records and historical CI/manual/Worker/release states. Add explicit Lab-Challenge associations gradually. Do not bulk-split current challenge files, change Flag values or change Worker APIs in this planning update.

capstone.purpose: A capstone path groups multiple standalone or progressive Challenges into a larger integrated assessment. It is a learning/aggregation object, not necessarily another independently graded Flag Challenge.
rules: A composite attack chain may be split into multiple learner-facing Challenges when each stage has a distinct learning objective, observable completion condition or useful knowledge outcome.
Challenges may have explicit prerequisite dependencies. A dependent Challenge is not falsely described as independently exploitable.
Use question-based completion for milestones whose natural outcome is knowledge or discovery and for which no authentic independent Flag exists.
Use a Flag only when the challenge objective has a naturally retrievable secret/goal; never add artificial flag files just to split a chain.
A capstone path groups child Challenges and may require all of them; it aggregates progress rather than duplicating a child Flag.
A Lab can host all child Challenges and the capstone path on one shared runtime; resetting the Lab affects all Challenges attached to that instance unless isolation is explicitly implemented.

flag_policy.principle: Challenge Flags are pedagogical checkpoints and are not constrained to the original machine's Flag count or placement.
rules: A Challenge may have its own Flag even when the original source machine had only one final Flag.
Place intermediate Flags in real application data or purpose-built challenge data surfaces that fit the stage's learning objective.
An intermediate Flag must be reachable through the intended stage and must not be publicly exposed, embedded in source delivered to learners, or trivially readable before the stage.
Do not add fake vulnerable endpoints, fake services or simulated exploit behavior merely to host a Flag.
A later-stage Flag should not be retrievable through an earlier-stage shortcut. Test all prior-stage routes against all later Flags.
The final Capstone aggregates child Challenge completion; it does not need a duplicate Flag unless it has a genuinely new objective.
Flags are Challenge data and are graded by the Web backend; Worker remains responsible only for Lab/sandbox lifecycle.

Progressive Challenge stages may each have their own Flag. Before adding one, test the actual privileges gained at that stage against all later-stage Flag locations; do not put a later Flag in a file readable by an earlier-stage foothold with the same OS identity.

progression.model: separate cumulative Challenge records sharing one Lab/target template
rules: Each learner-facing Challenge is a separate record and can be published/scored independently.
All cumulative Challenge records for one Lab bind to the same target template identifier.
Challenge 01 contains the first Flag stage; Challenge 02 repeats Flag 01 and adds Flag 02; Challenge 03 repeats Flag 01 and Flag 02 and adds Flag 03.
The later Challenge rechecks earlier milestones, so it is a full integrated assessment rather than only the final exploit stage.
A cumulative Challenge may repeat the same Flag answer in its own stage record; completion is tracked per Challenge stage, while the actual Lab data source may be shared.
Independent challenges with no prerequisite relation do not inherit previous Flags; they have their own goal and answer stages.
Do not add a separate Capstone entity for this pattern: the highest cumulative Challenge itself is the integrated challenge.

The Challenge records can share the same target template/image. Confirm whether runtime instance sharing is supported before promising one live container across simultaneously open Challenge pages; if starts create separate instances, the data/content model still shares the Lab template but not the live container.

lab_challenge_proposals.reason: Only Web stages are in scope for the Web curriculum; exclude SSH, Monit and sudo Root from these Challenge proposals.
Prefer one focused Challenge covering the reflected attribute context and cross-user browser behavior rather than splitting a single exploit into artificial questions.
Keep this as a focused beginner Challenge; multiple related XSS skills can be mapped to one Challenge.
Keep the existing composite challenge until the complete Web Flag path is accepted; its component skills can still be mapped to one Challenge.
Do not split or publish while the Lab's full development acceptance remains incomplete.

Create three separate Challenge records, all bound to the same NodeBlog target template/Lab. Each Challenge cumulatively includes the earlier Flag stages: Challenge 01 has 1 Flag; Challenge 02 has Flag 01 + Flag 02; Challenge 03 (integrated assessment) has Flag 01 + Flag 02 + Flag 03. This uses the existing ordered challenge_stages model and avoids requiring a separate Capstone entity. Prerequisites are reflected in the stages of each Challenge; the later Challenge intentionally rechecks earlier milestones.

stages.objective: Bypass the real MongoDB login query and access protected admin/article content.
Repeat/confirm the NoSQL authentication bypass prerequisite.
Use authenticated real libxml2 XXE to disclose the dedicated challenge-data Flag.
Use real node-serialize 0.0.4 deserialization to execute as NodeBlog service and retrieve the final Flag.
stages.flag_location: private MongoDB challenge record, not returned by ordinary routes

lab_challenge_proposals.reason: Careers ZIP upload, Shop SQLi, and the SQLi-created PHP include execution are distinct learning objectives/surfaces. Split the upload and SQLi into independent Challenges, and optionally split the file-write/include proof as a dependent Challenge. The final include stage has no safely isolated filesystem Flag while www-data can read the same file through the upload symlink; use an observable question answer for execution proof unless a robust non-bypassable answer store is designed.

challenges.title: Zipping 01 — ZIP Symlink File Disclosure
challenges.objective: Upload a single-entry Unix symlink ZIP and retrieve the intended target file through the returned document URL.
challenges.completion: Existing /home/rektsu/user.txt Flag; direct path confirmed by isolated runner.

challenges.title: Zipping 02 — SQL Injection and Database FILE
challenges.objective: Discover the shop product query, bypass the newline-sensitive filter, and use the real MariaDB query/FILE behavior to reach a database-specific answer.
challenges.completion: Add a distinct Flag in a dedicated database row/table reachable through the SQL injection query. This Flag confirms SQLi/DB access, not PHP execution.

challenges.title: Zipping 03 — SQLi File Write to PHP Include
challenges.objective: Use the SQLi FILE write path to create a PHP file and invoke it through the real shop include parameter.
challenges.completion: Question-based execution proof, e.g. submit the effective PHP execution identity or a stable output from the included PHP file. Do not reuse the ZIP-readable user.txt Flag. A separate Flag is deferred until a non-bypassable storage/retrieval boundary is proven.

challenges.title: Zipping — Complete Web Assessment
challenges.objective: Complete the independent upload and SQLi/file-include objectives on one shared Zipping Lab.
challenges.completion: Aggregate completion of child Challenges; no duplicate Flag.

lab_challenge_proposals.reason: The upload foothold, Nginx vhost/config discovery and WebSocket blind SQLi are three meaningful progressive learning objectives. Each can have a separate completion checkpoint. Use real target-local challenge data for the first two and retain the database-backed Web goal for the final stage; verify that the PHP upload identity cannot read the final DB goal.

challenges.title: Soccer 01 — File Manager Upload Foothold
challenges.objective: Discover the genuine Tiny File Manager 2.4.3 and establish the intended PHP upload foothold.
challenges.completion: Dedicated Flag in a root-owned seed copied to a www-data-readable, non-public challenge-data file or a protected application data record, reachable only after successful PHP execution in the upload directory.

challenges.title: Soccer 02 — Virtual Host and WebSocket Discovery
challenges.objective: Read the real Nginx configuration, identify soc-player.soccer.htb and discover the WebSocket ticket protocol.
challenges.completion: Distinct Flag/comment token in the actual Nginx vhost configuration, or a challenge-specific value in the config file. The first foothold permits local config reading, which is the intended behavior of this stage.

challenges.title: Soccer 03 — WebSocket Boolean Blind SQL Injection
challenges.objective: Use the ticket lookup oracle to extract the goal from the real MariaDB-backed account record.
challenges.completion: Existing Flag in soccer_db.accounts.goal; retain the root-owned 0400 seed and verify that the www-data foothold cannot read Node service source or DB credentials directly.

challenges.title: Soccer — Complete Web Assessment
challenges.objective: Complete the upload foothold, vhost/protocol discovery and WebSocket blind SQLi as one continuous assessment.
challenges.completion: Aggregate completion of child Challenges; no duplicate Flag.

lab_challenge_audit.scope: Source-level audit of existing NodeBlog, Zipping and Soccer Docker implementations, learner-facing challenge files, Flag storage and existing published CI evidence. No runtime code or challenge file was changed.
conclusions: A Lab can host multiple Challenges, but do not split a sequential exploit chain into separate Flag challenges unless each has a genuinely independent goal and naturally reachable answer.
A single Challenge can assess multiple Skills and can use question checkpoints before a final Flag stage.

The three audited Labs currently justify one composite Web Challenge each; Soccer has the clearest natural question checkpoints. Zipping has a likely unintended direct-Flag shortcut that must be tested before acceptance.

vulnerabilities.name: MongoDB operator authentication bypass
vulnerabilities.evidence: routes/login.js passes request objects directly into User.findOne; no fake query interpreter.

vulnerabilities.name: XXE file read/source disclosure
vulnerabilities.evidence: routes/articles.js invokes parseXmlString with noent:true and uses parsed XML fields.

vulnerabilities.name: Unsafe cookie deserialization RCE
vulnerabilities.entry: auth cookie parsed by authenticated() on normal requests
vulnerabilities.evidence: server.js calls serialize.unserialize before checking the MD5 signature.

flag.runtime: NODEBLOG_USER_FLAG is written at entrypoint, then unset before starting the app.
flag.reachability: The web process runs as nodeblog; final command execution through the real deserializer can read the Flag. Earlier auth/XXE stages disclose access and source but do not themselves read the Flag.

independence.decision: Keep one composite Challenge with three Skill mappings.
independence.reason: The stages are serial and the current implementation exposes only one final Web Flag. Separate Challenges would either need fabricated extra Flags or merely duplicate the same final goal. If useful, add question checkpoints (e.g. identify the vulnerable package/version) within the existing Challenge.

nodeblog.historical_ci: The README reports two fresh isolated instances with independent HTTP-only full Web chain verification. This is historical lab CI evidence, not manual acceptance or Worker verification.

vulnerabilities.name: ZIP symlink disclosure
vulnerabilities.real_component: PHP ZipArchive plus native Info-ZIP unzip
vulnerabilities.entry: POST /upload.php with one ZIP entry whose name ends in .pdf
vulnerabilities.evidence: upload.php extracts with unzip -j, renames the extracted entry into uploads, and Apache is configured with FollowSymLinks.

vulnerabilities.name: SQL injection with regex newline bypass
vulnerabilities.evidence: product.php applies a dot-based regex filter and interpolates the value into SQL; the PDO connection enables ATTR_EMULATE_PREPARES.

vulnerabilities.name: Database FILE write and PHP LFI/include
vulnerabilities.real_component: MariaDB FILE privilege and native PHP include
vulnerabilities.evidence: shop DB user has SELECT and FILE; index.php includes page+'.php' after file_exists.

flag.reachability: Confirmed direct read via the upload/symlink route: the same www-data-readable /home/rektsu/user.txt is exposed through Apache FollowSymLinks. The intended SQLi/LFI path also reaches it, but is not required.

independence.decision: Split into two Challenges by independent application surfaces: ZIP symlink file disclosure, and SQLi -> FILE write -> PHP include. Do not split SQLi, FILE write and LFI into separate Challenges because these stages are causally connected in the existing implementation.
independence.reason: The upload feature at /upload.php is independent of the shop product endpoint /shop/product.php and shop include endpoint /shop/index.php. The direct symlink Flag probe confirms the ZIP challenge has its own complete objective. The SQLi/FILE/LFI chain is a separate route; it needs a new distinct Flag/answer design before it can become a second publishable Challenge.

zipping.required_followup: Create a separate Challenge brief for the ZIP symlink disclosure using the confirmed existing path. Design a distinct second objective for SQLi -> FILE write -> PHP include; do not reuse the current Flag because it is already exposed by the ZIP route. Prove the second answer is retrievable through the SQLi/LFI chain and not by solving the ZIP Challenge alone. Then verify shared Lab reset/progress behavior in the platform.
zipping.historical_ci: The README reports two fresh isolated instances through symlink source read, SQLi filter bypass, MariaDB FILE write, PHP include and Flag retrieval. Existing CI evidence does not by itself rule out the shorter direct-symlink-to-Flag path.

probe_evidence.response: HTTP GET of the returned upload URL contained the unique test Flag
probe_evidence.scope: Disposable Ubuntu GitHub-hosted runner; isolated internal Docker network; unchanged Zipping image; temporary target; automatic cleanup.

vulnerabilities.name: Real PHP upload foothold
vulnerabilities.real_component: upstream Tiny File Manager 2.4.3 at pinned commit 1dbe7c5339ad955fcb08d01d256f591a3c83d713
vulnerabilities.evidence: Original upstream PHP file manager and move_uploaded_file handling; upload directory is executable.

vulnerabilities.name: Virtual-host/config disclosure
vulnerabilities.entry: Read Nginx config from the PHP foothold
vulnerabilities.evidence: Two Nginx vhosts are defined; second is soc-player.soccer.htb.

vulnerabilities.name: WebSocket boolean blind SQL injection
vulnerabilities.real_component: Node ws package and native MariaDB
vulnerabilities.evidence: server.js interpolates payload.id into SELECT id FROM tickets WHERE id = ...; true/false ticket responses form the oracle.

flag.reachability: startup inserts the seed value into MariaDB accounts.goal; the ticket_reader DB account can SELECT the database, and the WebSocket SQLi extracts the goal. The PHP foothold cannot read the root-owned seed file.

independence.decision: Keep one composite Challenge, add two question checkpoints before the final Flag.
independence.reason: Upload and vhost discovery are meaningful reconnaissance prerequisites, but they do not independently reach a Flag. The WebSocket SQLi is the final goal. Existing Challenge stages support question/flag kinds, so the learning milestones can be explicit without creating artificial separate Flag Challenges.

soccer.historical_ci: The README reports two fresh isolated instances solved over HTTP and WebSocket only, with distinct per-instance DB goal values. Worker and Web scoring integration remain unverified.

platform_reuse.observed: challenges has target_template_id; target_templates stores image, resources, variables and platform. Worker target requests and runtime records use target_id and owner_id; Worker is a lifecycle manager.
platform_reuse.not_proven: The inspected schema does not contain a Lab entity or LabChallenge association, and it does not prove that two different Challenge IDs for one user attach to the same running container or share reset/progress state.
platform_reuse.implication: Reusing one image/template across Challenges is already representable; reusing one live instance across multiple Challenges is a separate platform capability that must be verified before building multi-Challenge UX or changing Worker behavior.
platform_reuse.next_check: Trace the platform target-start API and target ID derivation, then test two Challenge IDs pointing at the same target template for one user. Confirm whether the runtime creates two target IDs/containers or a shared Lab instance. No Worker change is authorized by this audit.
